text:
maria: Heads-up — our SCIM sync from Okta started creating duplicate groups and some RBAC bindings show as broken after the sync. Noticed this in prod when a few engineers lost access.
aj: Do you have the SCIM/audit log lines? Which attribute are we using for group matching (externalId vs id)?
maria: We use externalId currently. Pasting relevant audit lines:```
2026-03-03T10:14:12Z INFO SCIM POST /Groups -> 201 created id=01fab234-exg, externalId=Engineering:Platform
2026-03-03T10:14:12Z INFO SCIM POST /Groups -> 201 created id=01fab235-exh, externalId=Engineering%3APlatform
2026-03-03T10:14:13Z ERROR SCIM POST /Groups -> 409 Conflict \"externalId already exists\" externalId=Engineering%20:Platform
```
maria: you can see slight variations in encoding/spacing. One record ended up created with a different externalId and our RBAC mappings referenced the canonical group id, so access broke.
tim: Okta sometimes sends mapped attribute with URL-encoding or different encode rules depending on app user settings. Also saw trailing whitespace come from an AD attribute.
aj: Can you confirm if these are coming from same Okta group id? If externalId isn't normalized we should either normalize upstream or change our matcher.
maria: They are the same Okta Source GUID in the Okta audit, but the SCIM payloads differ. Example payload snippets:```
POST /scim/Groups
{
  \"displayName\": \"Engineering:Platform\",
  \"externalId\": \"Engineering%3APlatform\"
}
```
j: (typo) aj: Suggest two mitigations: 1) normalize incoming externalId (url-decode + trim + lowercase) in SCIM consumer, 2) change SCIM mapping in Okta to send the normalized value (recommended).
olivia: Quick Okta mapping expression that helped us before: `String.urlDecode(trim(user.group.externalId)).toLowerCase()` — if you use custom expression, test in the Okta expression editor.
tim: I can also run a one-off dedupe script against the API to unify the duplicates. Example to map old -> canonical:```
# find duplicates by normalized externalId
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example.com/scim/Groups?filter=externalId%20eq%20\"Engineering%3APlatform\""
# PATCH canonical group to include members from dup id
curl -X PATCH -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example.com/scim/Groups/01fab234-exg" -d '{"members": [...]}'
```
maria: ran the dedupe for ~80% of the duplicates, one set failed with 412 Precondition Failed referencing `kv-checksum` in header.
sec-bot: Audit alert: KMS key rotation detected 2026-03-01T03:02Z. 24 SCIM payloads had a different wrapped token version. Suggest verify token unwrap logs in KMS.
maria: hmm we use KMS to encrypt some provisioning metadata (we store a signed externalId blob for integrity). If the key rotation changed the AEAD version we might not match signature when comparing externalId canonicalization.
aj: Two tracks: (A) patch SCIM consumer to decode+normalize before signature check so old wrapped tokens still map via unwrap+compare, (B) regen canonical blob for groups created post-rotation and do a controlled swap.
olivia: For short-term, change Okta mapping to send `id` (Okta GUID) instead of signed externalId; that'll avoid signed blob mismatch while we fix signature logic.
devops: Created ENGSEC-4287 and linked the actions: okta-mapping-change, dedupe-job, kms-unwrap-audit. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGSEC-4287
maria: thanks — switching Okta mapping now and will run the remaining dedupe over the next hour, will post results here.
tim: After dedupe, run RBAC reconcile: `POST /internal/rbac/reconcile?dry_run=false` to force mapping refresh.
maria: done, reconcile kicked off, looks good so far. will monitor for 24h and then close the jira. :thumbsup:
